properties.description: Moon (2009), directed by Duncan Jones and starring Sam Rockwell, Kevin Spacey and Dominique McElligott, is a low-budget, near-future science fiction drama that blends psychological mystery with emotional character work. Ultimately the story probes how ambition, memory, and self-deception shape a fractured identity.

The story chronicles personal grief, social hypocrisy, and the painful re-evaluation of identity against a meticulously rendered period backdrop.

properties.description: The Good Lie (2014), directed by Philippe Falardeau and starring Reese Witherspoon alongside Sudanese actors Arnold Oceng and Ger Duany, is a biographical drama about a group of young Sudanese refugees resettled in the United States. Its tone is simultaneously heartfelt and reflective, balancing moments of sorrow with dignity and quiet hope.

properties.description: Lust Stories (2018) is an Indian anthology film featuring four short films directed by Anurag Kashyap, Zoya Akhtar, Dibakar Banerjee and Karan Johar. The ensemble cast includes Radhika Apte, Bhumi Pednekar, Manisha Koirala, Vicky Kaushal, Kiara Advani, Sanjay Kapoor, Jaideep Ahlawat and Neha Dhupia. Across four distinct vignettes the film explores desire, infidelity, class tensions and female sexual agency in contemporary urban India. Tonally provocative and emotionally candid, it confronts social taboos around sex and gender while remaining character-driven and intimate.
properties.plot_summary: Four linked short films present intimate vignettes about desire, sex and emotional entanglement in contemporary urban India. One segment follows a married college professor who begins an affair with a younger student; another charts a housemaid’s complicated relationship with her employer. A third focuses on middle-aged infidelity and its ambiguous consequences, while the final story centers on a young woman asserting her sexual autonomy. Together the segments confront class, gender and social hypocrisy with frankness and emotional nuance.
properties.filming_location: St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, India, Mumbai, Maharashtra, India
properties.audience_identity: Adults who value candid, mature portrayals of sexuality and gender in contemporary society—open-minded, curious viewers interested in social issues, intimate character studies, and provocative storytelling.
properties.genre_description: An anthology of intimate, relationship-focused dramas that explore romantic and erotic aspects of modern life through multiple short-form narratives.
properties.style_description: The film favors intimate, naturalistic direction and close-up observation, using grounded domestic detail and candid performances to create a raw, reflective portrait of contemporary relationships.
